decision.explanation: The claim is supported by the provided evidence from the MyPathway study (pmid-29320312). The evidence confirms that in the subset of 14 NSCLC patients with somatic ERBB2 (HER2) mutations treated with the combination of trastuzumab and pertuzumab, there was an objective response activity with a partial response rate of 21% (3/14) and stable disease in an additional 3 patients for >120 days. This aligns with the claim's assertion of sensitivity/response in this specific molecular and disease context. While the evidence is from a small, uncontrolled basket trial subset, it directly supports the stated relationship between the therapy combination and the response in ERBB2-mutated NSCLC.

citations.quote: Fourteen of the 36 patients with HER2-mutated tumors had NSCLC (adenocarcinoma, n = 13; adenosquamous, n = 1); in this group, three patients (21%; 95% CI, 5% to 51%) had PR and three had SD > 120 days. Only one of the other 22 patients with HER2-mutated tumors responded to treatment with pertuzumab plus trastuzumab (biliary cancer).

The phase 2a MyPathway study assigned patients with HER2, EGFR, BRAF or SHH alterations to treatment with pertuzumab plus trastuzumab, erlotinib, vemurafenib, or vismodegib, respectively. Among thirty-six patients that received treatment with trastuzumab plus pertuzumab because of a HER2 mutation (without amplification/overexpression) four patients (11%; 95% CI, 3% to 26%) had objective responses.

unresolved: The evidence is limited to a small subset (n=14) within a multi-arm basket trial, lacking a control arm or statistical comparison to establish definitive predictive sensitivity relative to other therapies or wild-type status.
